newsitem.title: UK: BAe says no plans for GEC merger talks.
newsitem.headline: BAe says no plans for GEC merger talks.

text.p: British Aerospace denied on Thursday that it was about to get back into talks with The General Electric Co about merging their defence interests, but declined to rule out the idea in the longer term.

Chief executive Sir Richard Evans denied at a results news conference he was actively seeking to reopen the talks between Britain's two biggest defence groups now that former BAe executive George Simpson has taken the helm at GEC.
"It (trying to link with GEC) is not a priority," said Evans when asked if he was interested in reopening the talks, which last broke down publicly in 1993 after a leak to a newspaper.
"Nothing is in and nothing is out. We are where we are," Evans added.
"There are obviously a number of overlaps between the two companies...Whether they are sufficient to add up to mutuality and benefit to both sets of shareholders is a question we cannot answer."
Evans also said he believed Simpson would be too preoccupied getting to grips with such a large concern as GEC for there to be any chance of talks in the next 12 months.
And BAe was concentrating on moves to consolidate mainland Europe's defence and civil aerospace industries, he added.

Senior industry sources said earlier this month that British Aerospace believes a defence merger between itself and GEC makes strategic sense but was now more likely to come as part of a wider European-wide consolidation of the industry.

The sources said it was also suspected that the British Ministry of Defence wants to see GEC and BAe kept apart to maintain a modicum of domestic competition in the bidding for its own defence orders.
